<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אדר_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_93_D7_A8_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917334_theRebbe_880__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Israel's simple faith in G-dliness stems from two reasons: the soul's vision above intellect and the essential connection of the soul's essence to G-d, with the latter producing internal faith.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And this can be explained according to the known concept</t>
    <t s="2">that this that Israel believes in G-dliness with simple faith and does not need proofs for this is from two reasons.</t>
    <t s="3">Because their mazal sees.</t>
    <t s="4">For the soul above sees G-dliness</t>
    <t s="5">(a vision that is above intellect),</t>
    <t s="6">and this affects in the soul within the body the faith in G-dliness.</t>
    <t s="7">And additionally, an explanation:</t>
    <t s="8">that the root of faith is from the essence of the soul</t>
    <t s="9">(which is above "their mazal sees").</t>
    <t s="10">For this that the essence of the soul is connected to G-dliness is an essential connection</t>
    <t s="11">(which is not dependent on a cause,</t>
    <t s="12">nor even on the matter of vision that is above intellect).</t>
    <t s="13">And it can be said</t>
    <t s="14">that from the distinctions between the two explanations</t>
    <t s="15">(the concepts)</t>
    <t s="16">is,</t>
    <t s="17">that the faith in the soul clothed in the body that comes from the vision of the soul above is in the aspect of makif.</t>
    <t s="18">For since the soul above is above clothing, therefore its effect in the soul clothed in the body is in the aspect of makif.</t>
    <t s="19">And in order that the faith</t>
    <t s="20">(in the soul clothed in the body)</t>
    <t s="21">be internal,</t>
    <t s="22">it is through the revelation of the essential connection of the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="23">For the essence of the soul is the essence of the soul that is clothed in the body,</t>
    <t s="24">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="25">the faith of the soul clothed in the body that comes from the essence of the soul is in its inwardness.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the concepts of the maamar, explaining that Moshe's role as the faithful shepherd reveals the essence of the soul, which is the "light" that comes through the "crushing" of exile.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, the connection of the concepts in the maamar can be explained,</t>
    <t s="1">that the concept of</t>
    <t s="2">("crushed")</t>
    <t s="3">for the light comes after the explanation of the concept of Ra'aya Mehemna,</t>
    <t s="4">for this that Moshe nourishes and sustains the faith so that it be internal is through his revealing the essence of the soul</t>
    <t s="5">(which is above "their mazal sees"),</t>
    <t s="6">a light that is above light.</t>
    <t s="7">And what is written "crushed for the light,"</t>
    <t s="8">and it is explained in the maamar that in order to reach the light it is through the matter of "crushing" in the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="9">it is,</t>
    <t s="10">for the main revelation of the essence of the soul</t>
    <t s="11">(light)</t>
    <t s="12">is in the matter of mesirus nefesh</t>
    <t s="13">(whose primary time is in the time of exile),</t>
    <t s="14">as will be explained below.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the faith for which a Jew gives his life is specifically the faith stemming from the essence of the soul, which is his very self, making denial impossible.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And the concept is,</t>
    <t s="2">that this that the faith of Israel is in a manner that he gives his life for it,</t>
    <t s="3">it is</t>
    <t s="4">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="5">in the faith that comes from the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="6">For the faith from the aspect that he sees</t>
    <t s="7">("his mazal sees"),</t>
    <t s="8">although it is with great force</t>
    <t s="9">[as is known that the certainty that comes from sight is the greatest certainty],</t>
    <t s="10">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="11">since his faith is from a cause</t>
    <t s="12">(from the fact that he sees)</t>
    <t s="13">and is not connected to his own essential existence,</t>
    <t s="14">he is not compelled to give his life for it,</t>
    <t s="15">and this that the faith of Israel is in a manner that he gives his life for it is because faith in G-dliness is his very essence,</t>
    <t s="16">and therefore it is utterly impossible for him to deny it, G-d forbid.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
